templates.name: Discovery brief template
templates.what: The blank form for the Discovery brief, the first look at the requirement files. It lists the files, says which kind of file wins in a clash, and turns every gap into a question.
holds: 3. Known: what the sources say, topic by topic
4. Clashes, and how each is settled
Placeholders: What to write for each label

templates.name: Question log template
templates.what: The blank form for the Question log, the one list of every question the specifiers are asked in a project. Each question is rated for impact and severity and placed in a group that says how soon it must be answered.
filledBy: `grade-questions.cjs`: places each question in its group and sets the order
evidence: tools/grade-questions.cjs lines 9 and 32. It reads the grid from this template, its only home.

templates.name: BRD template
templates.what: The blank form for the BRD, the business case. It holds why the product is needed, what it must achieve, and the business requirements BR-01 onward.

templates.name: PRD template
templates.what: The blank form for the PRD. It holds every requirement the client stated, one per row, in simple words, with the client's own words and the source next to it.
holds: 4. Requirements: one part per source heading

templates.name: Things file template
templates.what: The blank form for the things file: the things a product keeps information about, found from its Glossary, one section per Glossary family. The file it makes is named {product}-glossary-things.md, not data-model-things.md.
holds: Status line and Next step line
Placeholders, with a City library example

templates.name: Data model file template
templates.what: The blank form for one Glossary family's data model file. For each thing it holds its actions, the rules for each field, and how it moves.
holds: Status line and Next step line
Placeholders, with a City library example: lending.md

templates.name: The data model's decisions file template
templates.what: The blank form for the data model's decisions file: every decision the data model asks, open or settled, and every Glossary change it needs. These decisions never go into the Question log.
holds: Placeholders, with the rules and a City library example
templates.checkedBy: `check-data-model.cjs`: run with the things file or a data model file

templates.name: Feature catalog template
templates.what: The blank form for the Feature catalog: the requirements turned into features in the Glossary's agreed words. Each feature has a priority, the FRD it belongs to, and a "Done when" line cut into numbered pieces.
holds: 2. Feature catalog: one part per PRD section heading

templates.name: EPIC grouping template
templates.what: The blank form for the EPIC grouping: the options for grouping features into EPICs, the one chosen, the clashes settled, and which EPICs get an EPIC brief. It is only ever added to.
holds: 3: Clashes, and how you settled them
3: EPIC brief list, in run order

templates.name: EPIC register template
templates.what: The blank form for the EPIC register: the list of EPICs, copied field for field from the chosen grouping, with their run order. It has no gate: it is accepted when its check passes.

templates.name: FRD template
templates.what: The blank form for one capability's FRD: the always-true "The system shall" rules, with the flow and the data they act on. Every "Done when" piece and every data model answer its features own is proved by at least one rule.
holds: Coverage — every Done-when piece has a rule
Coverage — every data model answer has a rule

templates.name: EPIC brief template
templates.what: The blank form for one EPIC described in full: its hypothesis, value, success measures, scope, features, dependencies and NFRs. It is written only for the EPICs the EPIC grouping's brief list marks Yes.

templates.name: Story list template
templates.what: The blank form for one EPIC's Story list: its stories in order, each with its statement and status, and which stories cover each feature.

templates.name: Story template
templates.what: The blank form for one Story, built up in one file: first its description, then its grooming, then its acceptance criteria. A Story has no status line.

templates.name: Change impact report template
templates.what: The blank form for one change, from the specifier's statement to the specifier's decision. Each of its 16 sections has exactly one writer, named under its heading. The file it makes is named impact-report.md, not change-impact-report.md.
holds: 1. The change, as you stated it
3. Other differences in a new version
4. Check findings on documents from outside
5. Restated, and split if several asks

templates.name: Decision record part
templates.what: The shape of the Decision record, the second-last section of every document that has a gate. Each entry records what the specifier decided and names its question.
holds: 5. The closing entry of a change
filledBy: Every skill that has a gate
`close-change.cjs`: the closing entry of a change
templates.checkedBy: none. Each document's own check program checks its Decision record.

templates.name: Version log part
templates.what: The shape of the Version log, the list of every accepted version of every document. Only a program writes it. Nobody edits it by hand.
holds: 1: one saved copy per accepted version

templates.name: Traceability map part
templates.what: The shape of the Traceability map, the file traceability-map.json that links every ID to the IDs it traces to. A program rebuilds it at every acceptance. Nobody edits it.

shared.name: `conventions.md`
shared.what: The rules every skill follows when it writes a document. It says who decides, the kinds of document, IDs, how every document opens, how unknowns are handled, and how templates and examples work.
holds: 14. A name is not a source
20. Running a skill on its own

shared.name: `simple-writing-rules.md`
shared.what: The writing rules every document follows, so a reader whose first language is not English understands it the first time. It also holds the word lists that the check program reads.
holds: The rule: every skill, every file, every time
readBy: `lib/check-document.cjs`: so every check program runs it

shared.name: `atomic-rules.md`
shared.what: The rules for one requirement per row: what one requirement is, when to split and when to keep together. Its check only lists rows to look at. It never fails, because only a person can judge a row.
holds: The rule: one requirement per row, in every document
2. When to split, and when to keep together

shared.name: `quality-characteristics.md`
shared.what: The ten yes-or-no tests, Q1 to Q10, that every unit a skill writes must pass. A skill names the tests by code and never copies the table.
evidence: .claude/skills/_shared/quality-characteristics.md line 7. It says check programs use it too. No program in tools/ names it.

shared.name: `decision-review-gates.md`
shared.what: The rules for every gate, the point where a skill hands its draft to the specifier for a decision. It covers what the specifier sees first, the order of questions, how each decision is put, and what happens after a third "no".
holds: Example: a decision at feature-author's gate, for Manager approval

shared.name: `project-folders.md`
shared.what: The map of a project's folders: where every document lives inside Output/{project}/, and which step writes it. Its JSON block is the only copy of the layout, and programs read it.
holds: 3. Every document's path: the JSON block of paths and the folders created at setup
readBy: `lib/run-paths.cjs`: so every skill and program finds files through it

shared.name: `data-model-design.md`
shared.what: Step-by-step instructions for writing one product's data model from its Glossary, BRD and PRD. Followed exactly, two runs on the same files give the same result.

glossaryMethod.name: Glossary method overview (`glossary-design.md`)
glossaryMethod.what: A short explanation of what the glossary method does and how its parts fit, for a first-time reader. It is not an instruction, and no skill or program reads it.
holds: Pointers to the docs that hold each rule
readBy: none: a page for people only

glossaryMethod.name: Method words (`method-words.md`)
glossaryMethod.what: The only file where the method's own words are defined, such as page, section, kind and relationship. Every glossary skill, template and prompt uses these words with these meanings only.

glossaryMethod.name: The three lenses and how they join
glossaryMethod.what: How the Glossary is built from the BRD and PRD, one section at a time, read three ways: what each section names, Ontology, what sits under what, Topology, and how things move, Choreography. `otc-methodology.md` sets the order and joins the lenses into the assembly draft.
holds: `otc-methodology.md`: the order the lenses run in, and how sections are joined
`lens1-ontology.md`: finds candidate words and what each means. It also holds the keep rule and how to write a definition.
`lens2-topology.md`: places each candidate in a tree
`lens3-choreography.md`: finds the states and flow of each candidate

glossaryMethod.name: The gate rules (`otc-run-rules.md`)
glossaryMethod.what: The judgments that need every section in view: which candidates qualify, how a weak word is improved, how conflicts are classed, how a re-run is reconciled, and who decides at each gate.
holds: Who decides at Gate 1 and Gate 2

glossaryMethod.name: Shapes and assembly of the Glossary pages

`glossary-assembly-principles.md`: the fixed layout of each of the seven glossary pages

`change-ripple.md`: every line still using a changed word
